name: API-Led Integration
description: A pattern for connecting systems through well-defined RESTful or GraphQL APIs with an API gateway managing access control, rate limiting, and versioning. Suitable for exposing internal capabilities to partners, other departments, or building microservice architectures with clear service boundaries.
whenToUse: Exposing internal capabilities to external partners or other government departments
Building a microservices architecture with clear bounded contexts and service contracts
Creating a platform where multiple consumers need controlled access to shared data or functions
Modernising legacy systems by wrapping them with API facades
Implementing an integration layer between disparate systems using standard protocols
whenNotToUse: Simple point-to-point integrations between two known systems with stable interfaces
Real-time streaming scenarios where request-response is inappropriate
Bulk data transfer scenarios better served by batch file exchange
Internal-only integrations where direct service-to-service calls are simpler
Scenarios where the overhead of API management is disproportionate to the integration complexity

typicalComponents.name: API Gateway
typicalComponents.purpose: Manage API access, authentication, rate limiting, and request routing
typicalComponents.technology: Amazon API Gateway, Azure API Management, or Apigee

typicalComponents.name: Backend Services
typicalComponents.purpose: Implement business logic behind API endpoints

typicalComponents.name: API Documentation Portal
typicalComponents.purpose: Publish API specifications and developer documentation

typicalComponents.name: Service Registry
typicalComponents.purpose: Track available services, versions, and health status
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Cloud Map, Azure Service Fabric, or Consul

typicalComponents.name: Monitoring and Analytics
typicalComponents.purpose: Track API usage, latency, error rates, and consumer behaviour
typicalComponents.technology: CloudWatch, Application Insights, or Cloud Monitoring

securityControls: Implement OAuth 2.0 or API key authentication for all API consumers
Apply rate limiting and throttling per consumer to prevent abuse
Validate all request payloads against published API schemas
Implement mutual TLS for service-to-service communication where required
Use API versioning to manage breaking changes without disrupting consumers
Log all API access with consumer identity for audit and forensics
resilienceConsiderations: Implement circuit breakers to prevent cascade failures across services
Design APIs to be idempotent for safe retry behaviour
Use asynchronous patterns for long-running operations with callback or polling
Implement request queuing for burst traffic handling
Deploy API gateway across multiple availability zones
Version APIs to allow graceful deprecation without breaking consumers
costConsiderations: API gateway costs scale with request volume — model expected traffic carefully
Multiple microservices increase compute and operational costs compared to monoliths
Developer portal and documentation maintenance requires ongoing investment
Consider the cost of API management platform licensing for enterprise features
Factor in the cost of consumer onboarding and support
operationalConsiderations: API versioning strategy must be defined and communicated to consumers
Consumer onboarding process needed for API key provisioning and documentation
SLA definitions required for each API tier (internal vs external consumers)
Monitoring must cover both API gateway metrics and backend service health
Deprecation policy needed for retiring old API versions
Contract testing between services to catch breaking changes early

services.purpose: API management for gRPC and REST services

questionsToAsk: Who are the API consumers and what are their authentication requirements?
What SLA commitments are needed for API availability and response times?
Is there a requirement for a public developer portal or is access restricted?
What API versioning strategy will be used (URL path, header, or query parameter)?
Are there existing API standards or design guidelines within the organisation?
What is the expected request volume and growth trajectory?
commonMistakes: Designing chatty APIs that require multiple round-trips for common operations
Not implementing proper API versioning from the start, making future changes painful
Exposing internal data models directly through APIs without proper abstraction
Neglecting to implement rate limiting, allowing a single consumer to overwhelm the service
Building a microservices architecture when a well-structured monolith would be simpler and cheaper
